A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Core Space merging work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support matching the equations, figures, tables and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original merging accuracy, timing, ablation and representation-analysis results for vision and language models in Section 5 and Appendices C and E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the vision, NLI, heterogeneous-rank and VeRA evaluations.

M1.justification: The reference-basis construction, projection, merging operator and reconstruction remain the same. v4 foregrounds direct projection in Equation (8), but this computation already appears in v1's Practical Implementation discussion and Listing 1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same eight vision datasets and six NLI datasets. Per-task vision evaluation and the task-unknown joint-class scenario are retained; no dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding tables retain the same comparator memberships: Full and KnOTS spaces, TA, TIES, DARE-TIES, TSV, CART, Iso-C and applicable +Iso-C combinations. The exclusions for NLI and comparator sets in the supplementary experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The checkpoint sources, backbones, adapter ranks, accuracy metrics and validation-based hyperparameter search remain unchanged. Table 7 retains identical hyperparameters, and the heterogeneous-rank and VeRA evaluation settings are preserved.

E4.justification: Both retain the truncation and subspace-alignment analyses, reference-basis ablation, embedding-interference comparison and merged-rank analysis in Figures 4–6 and Tables 5–6. No additional analytical question or supporting experiment is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, empirical error bars or significance tests. Reporting averages across tasks, samples or layers remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched empirical tables and plots retain their results. For example, Table 2 reports TSV-Core at 94.16% average normalized accuracy and 12 seconds in both versions, and Table 3 retains 76.43% for TSV+Iso-C in Core Space. Appendix Tables 8–10 are also numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: v4's core-matrix definition is algebraically equivalent to v1's aligned-core representation. The least-squares solutions, lossless-reconstruction arguments, linear-merging equivalence, generalized rank assumptions and Appendix A–B proofs and complexity derivations are retained; the exposition is rearranged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims of lossless shared-space representation, efficient integration with existing merging methods and strong vision/language performance. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations involving compactness, subspace alignment, interference and rank preservation remain substantively unchanged. Applicability to heterogeneous ranks and VeRA is retained, without new substantive limitations or failure conditions.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the projection transposes, and Listing 1 explicitly groups multiplication as (U_ref^T B)(A V_ref), matching the efficient order already described in v1's Appendix B. Commented alternative code is removed; hardware, hyperparameters, checkpoints and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Section 2 retains the same relationship to PEFT, existing merging algorithms and KnOTS, without new novelty claims or prior-work comparisons.

P1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 substantially reorganize the central method exposition around motivation, shared-basis projection and reparameterized merging. The formerly separate practical implementation and linear-merging discussions are integrated, core-matrix terminology is consolidated, and the redundant optimized-pipeline subsection in Appendix D is removed.

P2.justification: Figure 2's Core Space panel is redrawn as three labeled stages incorporating the existing optimized pipeline, replacing the separate Figure 7. Algorithm and listing layouts are revised, and appendix tables are relocated; the empirical plots and table structures remain largely stable.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the existing method easier to understand and reproduce by aligning Section 4.1 and Figure 2 with the direct implementation, correcting Algorithm 1's transposes and clarifying multiplication order in Listing 1. These changes reduce implementation ambiguity while preserving the empirical results and theoretical content, yielding a limited overall quality improvement.
